messages.subject: assert triggers in irace 2.2
messages.body_plain:
We have probably found a bug in irace 2.2 using R 3.2.3. In two projects of us each time after the second of three iterations completes the irace.assert(sum(nrow(iraceResults$experimentLog)) == experimentsUsedSoFar) fails within the irace function. messages.subject: Re: [irace-package] assert triggers in irace 2.2
messages.body_plain:
Dear Johannes,

Thanks for reporting this. The assert is detecting that the elements in
experimentLog are more than the number of experiments executed. I have now
analyzed that this happens because we record in experimentLog experiments that
are actually not executed (because they are elitist and we re-use a previous
result). I have long suspected this may be the case when target-evaluator is
used (since target-evaluator is always invoked but target-runner is sometimes
not if we have already done the same experiment), but I couldn't reproduce it,
so thanks again for reporting this.

For the final user, the only thing wrong is the data structure experimentLog,
which is just a log and not really used by irace for computations or deciding
when to stop. Thus, if you don't use this log for further analysis, you may
simply comment out the assert. You may also downgrade to irace 2.1, but
experimentLog may also be wrong there.

I'm preparing a more thorough fix so that experimentLog is correct, but it may
take some days to reach CRAN.

Best wishes,

Manuel.

messages.subject: irace 2.3
messages.body_plain:
Dear irace users,

Version 2.3 of irace is available from CRAN: https://cran.r-project.org/package=irace

This releases fixes a minor bug that triggers an internal assertion.

 * Fix bug that will cause iraceResults$experimentLog to count calls to
   targetEvaluator as experiments, even if no call to targetRunner was
   performed. This does not affect the computation of the budget consumed and,
   thus, it does not affect the termination criteria of irace. The bug triggers
   an assertion that terminates irace, thus no successful run with version 2.2
   is affected.

Best wishes,

Manuel López-Ibáñez.

messages.subject: Re: [irace-package] Irace with a big range
messages.body_plain:
Dear Matthieu,

Short answer: It is better to declare it as an integer.

Long answer: The details of the current implementation are explained in the ORP
paper. In a nutshell, integer parameters are treated as real and then rounded
back to integers. However, the rounding is non-trivial (see footnote 2), thus
it is better to let irace handle it.

Cheers,

	Manuel.
